stemBlocks.value: A farm's banana production, to the nearest tonne, was: 2010 → 150, 2011 → 275, 2012 → 100, 2013 → 40, 2014 → 125, 2015 → 210. (a) Draw a bar chart using 1 cm to 1 year on the x-axis and 1 cm to 25 tonnes on the y-axis. (b) Determine the range of the production between 2010 and 2015. (c)(i) In which year was production greatest, and (ii) how is that shown on the bar chart? (d)(i) Between which two consecutive years was the change in production greatest, and (ii) how is that shown on the bar chart?
Think first: Every part here is read from the same six numbers, so work with the table and treat the bar chart as a picture of it.

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the range by subtracting the smallest value from the largest.
Identify the year with the greatest production.
Work out the change between each pair of consecutive years.

contentBlocks.value: Result: The largest change is 175 tonnes, between 2011 and 2012

strategyBlocks.value: Plot one bar per year to the given scale, subtract the smallest production from the largest for the range, then compare the six values (and the differences between consecutive values) to answer the reading questions.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) A bar chart with six equal, separated bars of heights 150, 275, 100, 40, 125 and 210 tonnes (1 cm = 25 tonnes).  (b) Range = 275 − 40 = 235 tonnes.  (c)(i) 2011  (ii) It is the tallest bar on the chart.  (d)(i) Between 2011 and 2012 (a fall of 175 tonnes)  (ii) It is the largest difference in height between two neighbouring bars.

whyThisWorks.value: A bar chart converts each number into a length, so comparisons of size become comparisons of height. The range measures the spread of the data by using only the two extreme values, which on the chart are simply the tallest and shortest bars. Change between consecutive years is a difference, and a difference shows up as a step in height between adjacent bars.

commonErrors.misconception: Giving the range as '40 to 275' instead of a single number, 235 tonnes.

commonErrors.misconception: Reading the greatest change as the change to or from the tallest bar, rather than comparing all five consecutive differences.

examTip.value: When a question says 'greatest change', list all the consecutive differences in a line before choosing — the biggest bar and the biggest change are usually not the same pair.
